answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to earn trust through a chain of useful work: before transacting, it must complete small verifiable tasks for established peers, each leaving a signed receipt. Like a comet that only gains a tail by passing close to a star, an agent's reputation grows only through real interaction; a lone vertex with no receipts stays an island, unable to receive payments. Forging thousands of fake identities is pointless because each must independently pay the time and compute cost of real work, while one honest history compounds into cheaper access.
